sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports and project location
sections.what: Loads the file and path tools, loads the prepared wind data, and works out the project's root folder so other paths can be built from it.
sections.why: Needed so the script can read the data files and write the report in the right place.
sections.watch_out: The prepared data is read at the start, so the script fails immediately if that file is missing or moved.

sections.name: load, esc, table, domains, verifiedFields
sections.title: Helpers for loading files and building tables
sections.what: Reads named result files from the data folder, and prefers the initial commit file when it exists. It also provides a function that makes text safe for HTML, a function that builds HTML tables, and sets that collect publisher domains and verified field names.
sections.why: Likely reason: the same steps repeat across the page, so they are kept in one place.
sections.watch_out: The escaping step protects the page from broken markup when a quotation contains symbols, so removing it would break the layout.

sections.name: registerStates (part 1)
sections.title: Headline counts and the top of the page
sections.what: Counts how many references are in each verification state and how many report claims are uploaded-only. It then writes the page header, the warning that this is not universal original-source verification, and the reconciliation and measured-coverage tables.
sections.why: Likely reason: the headline figures are meant to come from the data so the page matches the saved results.
sections.watch_out: Some numbers in this part are typed in as fixed text, such as the 13 and 11 counts, so they will not update if the data changes.

sections.name: registerStates (part 2)
sections.title: Rest of the page and saving the file
sections.what: Adds the financial decisions, the full reference register, the evidence for each field, the company roles, and the audit section. It then checks the page is under 5 MiB, creates the reports folder if needed, writes the HTML file, and prints the size.
sections.why: Writing the whole page in one step lets the size limit be checked before anything is saved.
sections.watch_out: If the size limit is exceeded the script throws an error and writes nothing, and several lines in this part were cut off in the packet, so their content is unclear.

summary: Builds a single HTML page that summarises the wind import: what was added, how well it is backed by original sources, and what is still unverified.
purpose: Produces the reviewer-facing reconciliation report for the wind import batch, saved at reports/wind-import-reconciliation.html.
why: Likely reason: lets a reviewer check claims, quotations and source links in a web browser without needing database access.
how: Loads the prepared wind data and the saved results from data/wind. It counts reference verification states, uploaded-report claims and verified excerpts, then builds the page section by section with tables and expandable details. It checks the page is under 5 MiB, creates the reports folder if needed, writes the HTML file, and prints the byte count.
inputs: The prepared wind data file under src/ingest/wind, and the JSON result files in data/wind: commit, initial-commit (used when present), verification, live-verification, and browser-fix-verification (optional).
outputs: reports/wind-import-reconciliation.html, and one console line giving the size in bytes.
risks: Many headline numbers and sentences are typed directly into the page text, such as the 13 and 11 counts, the 112 unretrieved references, and the 9 passed test groups, so they will not update if the data changes. The script stops with an error if any required data file is missing, and it refuses to write a page larger than 5 MiB. Several lines in the packet were cut off, so parts of the page content could not be checked.
debug: If the script fails on load, check that every file in data/wind named above exists. If the page numbers look wrong, compare the typed-in text with the figures in the JSON files. If the size error appears, look for unusually long quotations or an unusually large evidence list.
